findings.found: android:debuggable="true" on <application>: the build can be debugged on any device, and app stores do not accept a debuggable app
findings.fix: remove android:debuggable from the manifest; the build tools set it for debug builds only

basis.text: android:debuggable says whether the app can be debugged even on a device in user mode, and it is false by default
a debuggable app lets an attacker debug it and reach parts of it that should stay closed, so the flag must be false in the build that ships

findings.own: only the literal value true counts; a resource reference such as @bool/debug or a manifest placeholder is not resolved

findings.found: android:usesCleartextTraffic="true": every connection of the app may use cleartext HTTP; on Android 7.0 and higher the network security config @xml/network_security_config decides instead
findings.fix: set android:usesCleartextTraffic="false" and cleartextTrafficPermitted="false" in the base-config, and use HTTPS; allow cleartext only to a named domain that needs it

basis.text: android:usesCleartextTraffic is true by default up to target API level 27 and false from 28, and a network security config decides instead on API level 24 and higher

a network security config sets cleartextTrafficPermitted and the trusted certificate authorities for the whole app in base-config and per domain in domain-config, and debug-overrides apply only to debuggable builds
cleartext traffic can be read and changed by anyone on the network path, so data should go over encrypted channels, with cleartext opted out in the network security config

findings.own: android:usesCleartextTraffic="true", a base-config with cleartextTrafficPermitted="true", or a targetSdkVersion below 28 written in the manifest with neither of the two set to false; a target API level set only in the Gradle build is not seen

findings.found: <activity android:name=".DeepLinkActivity"> has an <intent-filter> and no android:exported: the app cannot be installed on Android 12 and higher, and on older systems the component is exported
findings.fix: set android:exported explicitly: true only when other apps must start the component, false otherwise

basis.text: an activity, service or broadcast receiver with an intent filter and no explicit android:exported cannot be installed on Android 12 or higher

basis.text: the default of android:exported differed between versions and kinds of component, so it should always be set, or internal components may be exposed to other apps

findings.own: an activity, activity-alias, service or receiver with an intent-filter and no android:exported; an error, because the app cannot be installed on Android 12 and higher
